record.title: Period-$2m$ conjecture for arithmetic-progression Max-Welter positions
record.statement:
Let $a\geq 0$, $m\geq 1$, and $k\geq 1$. Then the sequence

$$
\{\mathcal{G}(a+i,a+m+i,\ldots,a+km+i)\}_{i\geq 0}
$$

is ultimately periodic with period $p=2m$. This conjectures periodicity of the Sprague–Grundy values for positions whose coordinates form an arithmetic progression with common difference $m$.
record.source_name: Nhan Bao Ho, “The game Max-Welter”, arXiv:1202.4075 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.4075

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2012).

record.title: The alternating-circuit bound for balanced red-blue graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a balanced red-blue graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. An **alternating-circuit bound** asserts that

1. there exists an alternating circuit of length at most $3n^2/m$; and
2. $\mathbf{maxC}_u(G)\ge m^2/(6n^2)$.

Such an upper bound would provide a lower bound on the swap-distance and could therefore be useful in practical applications.
record.source_name: Péter L. Erdős, Zoltán Király and István Miklós, “On the swap-distances of different realizations of a graphical degree sequence”, arXiv:1205.2842 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.2842

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2012).

record.title: Conjecture on the value of the fractional precoloring extension threshold at distance 7
record.statement:
Let $g(k,d)$ denote the fractional precoloring extension threshold for distance $d$ as defined in the paper. **Distance-7 value conjecture.** For $k\in[2,2.5)$,

$$
g(k,7)=\dfrac1{k^2-k+1},
$$

while for $k\in[2.5,3)$,

$$
g(k,7)=\dfrac1{k+1}.
$$

The authors believe their upper bounds for $g(k,d)$ are tight; this conjecture concerns the case $d=7$ and remains open in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Jan van den Heuvel, Daniel Kral, Martin Kupec, Jean-Sebastien Sereni and Jan Volec, “Extensions of Fractional Precolorings show Discontinuous Behavior”, arXiv:1205.5405 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.5405

record.title: Four-variable Rado number conjecture for $x+a(x+y)=2aw$
record.statement:
Let $a$ be a positive integer, and let $R(x+a(x+y)=2aw)$ denote the 2-color Rado number of the four-variable equation $x+a(x+y)=2aw$. **Four-variable Rado number conjecture.**

$$
R(x+a(x+y)=2aw)=a^2.
$$

The conjecture proposes an extension of the previously determined three-variable equation $x+ay=2az$; the supplied text gives no resolution evidence.
record.source_name: William Gasarch, Russel Moriarty and Nithin Tumma, “New Upper and Lower Bounds on the Rado Numbers”, arXiv:1206.4885 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.4885

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2012).

record.title: Nonexistence conjecture for hoppers of levels 1 and 2
record.statement: A **hopper of level 1 or 2** is the corresponding hopper object defined in the paper's graph-embedding framework. **The no-hoppers conjecture.** There are no hoppers of level 1 or 2. The source states this as a suspicion following the Mohar–Škoda conjecture and gives no evidence of resolution, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Bojan Mohar and Petr Škoda, “Obstructions of Connectivity 2 for Embedding Graphs into the Torus”, arXiv:1207.6126 (2012).

record.title: The k(k−3)-certificate conjecture for perfect matchings
record.statement: Under the paper's setup, $H$ is a $k$-graph satisfying the stated setup hypotheses, and a $C$-certificate is the obstruction defined there. **The $k(k-3)$-certificate conjecture.** $H$ has a perfect matching if and only if there is no $k(k-3)$-certificate for $H$. A proof would improve the running time of the paper's main algorithm.
record.source_name: Peter Keevash, Fiachra Knox and Richard Mycroft, “Polynomial-time perfect matchings in dense hypergraphs”, arXiv:1307.2608 (2014).
record.references:

record.title: Frankl's bipartite graph conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph with at least one edge, and consider its two bipartition classes. A vertex is **low-frequency** if it lies in at most half of the maximal stable sets of $G$.

**Frankl's graph conjecture.** Each bipartition class of $G$ contains a low-frequency vertex.

This is described as a reformulation of the union-closed sets conjecture. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Henning Bruhn and Oliver Schaudt, “The journey of the union-closed sets conjecture”, arXiv:1309.3297 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.3297

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2013).

record.title: Jockusch's edge lower-bound conjecture for cubical polytopes
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a cubical polytope of dimension $d\geq 3$, with $V$ vertices and $E$ edges. **Jockusch's conjecture.**

$$
E\geq \frac{d+1}{2}V-2^{d-1}.
$$

The source attributes this conjecture to Jockusch and discusses partial results toward it.
record.source_name: Gil Kalai, Eran Nevo and Isabella Novik, “Bipartite Rigidity”, arXiv:1312.0209 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.0209

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2013). “At present, even the inequality $E\leq 3|V(G)|-9$ of the above conjecture is open. (Equality $|E|=3|V|-9$ holds for complete bipartite graphs $K_{3,m}$; these graphs are apex graphs, and hence linklessly embeddable.”

record.title: Complete transitivity conjecture for the codes $C^{(i)}$
record.statement:
Let $C^{(i)}$ be the nested binary codes defined in the paper, with parameter $u$ and $i
ein\{0,1,\ldots,u\}$. **Complete transitivity conjecture.** The code $C^{(i)}$ is completely transitive if and only if $i=0$, $i=1$, $i=u$, or $2^i\leq u+1$ for $i\in\{2,\ldots,u-1\}$. This conjecture requires determining the exact automorphism group of each $C^{(i)}$; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: J. Borges, J. Rifà and V. A. Zinoviev, “Families of nested completely regular codes and distance-regular graphs”, arXiv:1404.6358 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.6358

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2014).

record.title: The domination conjecture for symmetric biplanes
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a symmetric $(v,k,2)$-design with $k\geq 4$, and let $\gamma(D)$ denote the domination number of its incidence graph.

**Biplane domination conjecture.**

$$
\gamma(D)=k.
$$

General bounds established earlier in the paper give an upper bound for $\gamma(D)$ in this setting, while the asserted equality remains open for symmetric $(v,k,2)$-designs with $k\geq 4$.
record.source_name: Felix Goldberg, Deepak Rajendraprasad and Rogers Mathew, “Domination in designs”, arXiv:1405.3436 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.3436

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2014). “Finally, a number of open questions are proposed.”

record.title: Conjecture on consecutive extremal-prime ratios
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb E=(e_k)_{k\geq 1}$ be the sequence of extremal prime numbers, listed in increasing order. **Consecutive-ratio conjecture.** In this notation,

$$
\lim_{k\rightarrow \infty}\frac{e_{k+1}}{e_k}=1.
$$

The conjecture is supported by the paper's numerical data, but no proof or disproof is supplied.
record.source_name: Edward Tutaj, “Prime numbers with a certain extremal type property”, arXiv:1408.3609 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.3609

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2014).

record.title: Cyclic Young graph conjecture for the family in $Z_{2n-1}$
record.statement:
Let $Y(g,k)$ be a Young graph, and let $Z_m$ denote the equivalence class of cyclic Young graphs on $m$ nodes. **Cyclic Young graph conjecture.** For $t\ge 3$ and $n\ge 2$, the Young graph

$$
Y((n^2+n)t-n^2+n+1, n^2t-(n-1)^2)
$$

is in $Z_{2n-1}$. This is an experimentally suggested structural pattern for cyclic Young graphs; the source gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: L. H. Kendrick, “Young Graphs: 1089 et al”, arXiv:1410.0106 (2015).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2014). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1307.0453](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.0453).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.0106

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2014).

record.title: Minimal-energy equality conjecture for three, four and five partitions of the square torus
record.statement:
Let $\mathsf{T}(1,1)$ be the square flat torus. Let $\mathsf{H}_3(1)$ and $\mathsf{H}_4(1)$ be the hexagonal tiling domains appearing in Proposition 1, and let $\mathsf Q$ be the square of side $1/\sqrt{5}$ used as the tiling domain of a $5$-partition. The proposition gives

$$
\mathfrak{L}_3(\mathsf{T}(1,1))\leq\lambda_1(\mathsf{H}_3(1)),\qquad
\mathfrak{L}_4(\mathsf{T}(1,1))\leq\lambda_1(\mathsf{H}_4(1)),
$$

and

$$
\mathfrak{L}_5(\mathsf{T}(1,1))\leq\lambda_1(\mathsf Q)=10\pi^2.
$$

**Minimal-energy equality conjecture.** The three inequalities in Proposition 1 are equalities.

If true, these candidates would give the exact minimal energies for $3$-, $4$- and $5$-partitions of the square torus. The statement is presented as a conjecture, with only the displayed upper bounds established in the source.
record.source_name: Virginie Bonnaillie-Noël and Corentin Léna, “Spectral minimal partitions for a family of tori”, arXiv:1503.04545 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.04545

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2015).

record.title: Normalized Vafa–Witten partition functions satisfy S-duality
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a smooth projective surface, let $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$, and let $\eta(q)=q^{1/24}\prod_{k\geq 1}(1-q^k)$ be the Dedekind eta function. Define the normalized partition function by

$$
\widehat{Z}(\operatorname{SU}(r);q)=\eta(q)^{-w}Z(\operatorname{SU}(r);q).
$$

Define the analogous normalized partition function for $\operatorname{SU}(r)/{\mathbb Z}_r$. **Normalized S-duality conjecture.** The normalized partition functions satisfy

$$
\widehat{Z}\left(\operatorname{SU}(r);-\frac{1}{\tau}\right)=\pm r^{-\frac{\chi}{2}}\widehat{Z}(\operatorname{SU}(r)/{\mathbb Z}_r;\tau).
$$

This is the eta-normalized form of the Vafa–Witten S-duality prediction, in which the modular-weight factor is removed. The paper relates these functions to invariants of moduli spaces of Gieseker-stable Higgs sheaves but leaves the conjecture open in general.
record.source_name: Yunfeng Jiang, “Counting twisted sheaves and S-duality”, arXiv:1909.04241 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.04241

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2019).

record.title: Minimal unbounded-bb classes in hereditary graph classes
record.statement: A graph class is **minimal of unbounded $\lambda$** if it has unbounded $\lambda$, while every proper hereditary subclass has bounded $\lambda$. **Minimal-class conjecture for $\lambda$.** Every graph class of unbounded $\lambda$ contains a minimal class of unbounded $\lambda$. The paper presents this as an analogue of the established statement for $\gamma$ and does not resolve it.
record.source_name: Bogdan Alecu and Vadim Lozin, “Understanding lettericity I: a structural hierarchy”, arXiv:2106.03267 (2021).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.03267

record.title: Kühn–Osthus conjecture for strongly 2-connected regular digraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a strongly $2$-connected $d$-regular digraph on $n$ vertices, where

$$
d\geq n/3.
$$

**Kühn–Osthus conjecture.** The digraph $G$ contains a Hamilton cycle. The source introduces this as the digraph analogue of the $t=2$ case of the Bollobás–Häggkvist conjecture; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Allan Lo, Viresh Patel and Mehmet Akif Yıldız, “Hamilton Cycles in Dense Regular Digraphs and Oriented Graphs”, arXiv:2203.10112 (2023).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.10112

record.title: Revised Kempe-class conjecture for almost bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph formed from a bipartite graph $B$ by adding $\ell$ edges, so that $G$ is a $(k-1)$-colorable $B+E_\ell$ graph. For a graph $G$ and positive integer $k$, let $\operatorname{Kc}(G,k)$ denote the number of equivalence classes of $k$-colorings, where two colorings are equivalent if one can be transformed into the other by a sequence of Kempe swaps. Let $\mathbf{1}_{k-1}$ denote the indicator of the relevant condition on $k-1$ as used in the source.

**Revised Kempe-class conjecture.** If $G$ is a $(k-1)$-colorable $B+E_\ell$ graph with $k\geq 4$ and

$$
\ell<\frac{k^2+8k-45+\mathbf{1}_{k-1}}{4},
$$

then

$$
\operatorname{Kc}(G,k)=1.
$$

This is proposed as a revised version after the original conjecture was disproved in part of its range. The supplied text does not state whether the revised conjecture has been proved or refuted.
record.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston and Carl Feghali, “Kempe Classes and Almost Bipartite Graphs”, arXiv:2303.09365 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.09365

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2023). “For all $k\ge 8$, Conjecture is false.”

record.title: Maximal-minus-minimal homomesy conjecture for products of two chains
record.statement:
Let $P=[m]\times[n]$ be the product of two chains, and let $\mathcal{IC}(P)$ denote its interval-closed sets. Rowmotion acts on $\mathcal{IC}(P)$. For an interval-closed set, consider the statistic given by the number of maximal elements minus the number of minimal elements. A statistic is $0$-mesic if its average over every rowmotion orbit is zero.

**Maximal-minus-minimal homomesy conjecture.** The number of maximal elements minus the number of minimal elements is $0$-mesic under rowmotion on $\mathcal{IC}(P)$ for $P=[m]\times[n]$.

The conjecture was tested on all products of two chains with $m+n\leq 12$. The paper notes that the analogous statistic is not homomesic for the products $[2]\times[2]\times[5]$ and $[2]\times[2]\times[2]\times[2]$, while the conjecture for two chains remains open.
record.source_name: Jennifer Elder, Nadia Lafrenière, Erin McNicholas, Jessica Striker and Amanda Welch, “Toggling, rowmotion, and homomesy on interval-closed sets”, arXiv:2307.08520 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08520

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2023). “This paper contains several conjectures and open problems.”

record.title: Alspach et al.'s wreath-product conjecture for hamiltonian decomposable digraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be hamiltonian decomposable directed graphs. Their **wreath product** $G \wr H$ is the digraph on vertex set $V(G)\times V(H)$ with an arc from $(g_1,h_1)$ to $(g_2,h_2)$ if and only if there is an arc from $g_1$ to $g_2$ in $G$, or there is an arc from $h_1$ to $h_2$ in $H$ and $g_1=g_2$. A directed graph is **hamiltonian decomposable** if it admits a decomposition into directed hamiltonian cycles.

**Alspach et al.'s wreath-product conjecture.** If $G$ and $H$ are hamiltonian decomposable directed graphs, then $G\wr H$ is also hamiltonian decomposable.

This is a long-standing conjecture for directed graphs, first appearing in Alspach et al. (1987). The paper affirms most of its previously open cases, but the supplied text does not establish that every case has been resolved.
record.source_name: Alice Lacaze-Masmonteil, “Hamiltonian decompositions of the wreath product of hamiltonian decomposable digraphs”, arXiv:2412.13392 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2410.02109](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.02109).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.13392

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).

record.title: Packing-covering conjecture for infinite matroids
record.statement: For any family of matroids on the same ground set, there is a partition of the ground set into two parts, the packing side and the covering side, such that the family obtained by contracting each matroid onto the packing side has a packing, and the family obtained by restricting each matroid to the covering side has a covering. Here, a packing consists of a disjoint family of bases, one from each matroid, and a covering consists of a family of bases, one from each matroid, whose union is the whole ground set.
